source.title: Four Things Everyone Should Know to Improve Batch Normalization

record.tranche_reason: Tests Ghost Batch Normalization as a generalization aid in medium-batch image classification, extending the normalization/regularization conditions in V5. It does not test the fixed-epoch large-batch comparison directly.
record.gate_note: Ghost Batch Normalization results bear on V5. Other normalization improvements and cited large-batch findings do not directly test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures improvements from normalization changes, including varying normalization subset size within a training batch. It does not compare larger versus smaller optimization batches under fixed epoch budgets or demonstrate mitigation of a measured large-batch penalty. Its large-batch generalization-gap evidence is cited prior work. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the Ghost Batch Normalization findings, but only part of the authors' conclusion. They present four normalization improvements: inference example weighing, Ghost Batch Normalization for medium batches, weight decay on normalization scale and shift parameters, and combined Batch/Group Normalization for small batches. Their benefits depend on the method, architecture, dataset, and batch setting; Ghost Batch Normalization provides no improvement on their SVHN setting.
record.recipe_differences: Changes normalization during training by splitting batches into ghost subsets; does not compare large and small batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and Ghost Batch Normalization size affect accuracy; the authors describe a unimodal relationship with best performance at an intermediate ghost size.

fits_no_version.finding: Ghost Batch Normalization improves validation accuracy by 0.84 percentage points on CIFAR-100 and 5.8 points on Caltech-256, with no improvement over the 98.79% SVHN baseline. Intermediate normalization subset sizes perform best.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tuning normalization subset size within a fixed optimization batch can improve image-classification generalization, with benefits depending on the dataset and regularization strength.

record.problems: The relevant Ghost Batch Normalization accuracy curves are figure-based, and the text does not provide exact batch settings or uncertainty for these comparisons. It reports validation outcomes, not train-test error gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No other relevant rows omitted. The paper cites prior large-batch generalization-gap results but those are not its own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Optimization-batch size effects under fixed epoch budgets and mitigation of a measured large-batch penalty.

Adding dropout, excessive dropout, small-training-set exceptions, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation. Weight decay on normalization parameters alone does not test these comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparison against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: Here, cannot_determine means the rows cannot establish any listed version's effect; the reported normalization gains and null result remain valid. Figure 5 explicitly uses ghost batch size for the Ghost Batch Normalization curve and an idealized constant Batch Normalization baseline, so it supplies no missing direct V5 comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
No direct comparison of large and small batch training under a fixed epoch budget; no language models or learning-rate warmup study.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varied Ghost Batch Normalization size; validation accuracy peaked at an intermediate size.
rows.value: Improved performance by 0.84% with Ghost Batch Normalization.
rows.note: Text reports the gain but does not identify the ghost batch size producing it or give the baseline accuracy.
rows.check: The 0.84 percentage-point validation accuracy gain is correctly reported, but changing ghost batch size measures normalization regularization rather than V5's optimization-batch penalty. Section 4.2 identifies an overall batch size of 128 for the related end-to-end experiments; it should not be silently substituted for an unspecified Figure 3 setting.

rows.subject: Inception-v3
rows.operation_detail: Varied Ghost Batch Normalization size; validation accuracy peaked at an intermediate size.
rows.value: Improved performance by 5.8% with Ghost Batch Normalization.
rows.note: Text reports the gain but does not identify the ghost batch size producing it or give the baseline accuracy.
rows.check: The 5.8 percentage-point validation accuracy gain is correctly reported. It compares normalization configurations, without a measured large-versus-small optimization-batch penalty or fixed-epoch mitigation comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.value: Ghost Batch Normalization did not result in an improvement.
rows.note: Authors connect the null result to the already high baseline and low overfitting.
rows.check: The 98.79% baseline and lack of improvement are correctly reported. This null normalization benefit cannot establish absence of V5's batch-size penalty or limit the scope of its mitigation clause.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
